rationale: All four blocking findings resolved, no new findings, so the gate approves. CR-001: health-check payload now collapses a blank wiki to undefined, matching the create request. CR-002: applyHealthCheckFieldError maps the backend's 'space' onto xwikiSpace and anchors 'url' — a credential field with no input on this form — to the integration selector, carrying the backend's /rest vs /xwiki/rest help text; both paths mutation-verified (reverting to the old direct setError call fails both tests). CR-003: the update path now sends DEFAULT_XWIKI_WIKI explicitly, since an omitted wiki means 'keep the stored value' server-side. CR-004: a new hook-level suite (9 tests) covers create omission, the full update path including the clear-to-default case, the health-check payload, and the field-error routing; the integration suite additionally asserts the serialized create and health bodies both omit wiki. No confirmation-pass lens dispatch was needed: the fix-up diff is 384 lines, mostly tests, and the one suspicion it raised was resolved by direct verification rather than deferred. That suspicion was self-inflicted scope creep — the first cut of HEALTH_CHECK_FIELD_MAP also mapped wiki_query/wiql_query, silently changing error-highlighting for Azure DevOps datasources from an xWiki ticket. Enumerating every field_error the backend can emit (space, url, git_url, svn_repo_url, jql, cql, wiki_query, wiql_query) confirmed the overreach, and the map was pulled back to the two xWiki fields with a comment recording that the other four mismatches are pre-existing and deliberately untouched. Two process notes for the record: an over-strict assertion in the first draft of the hook test (`not.toHaveProperty('wiki')` on the in-memory object, where `wiki: undefined` leaves the key present but JSON.stringify drops it) was corrected to assert wire behaviour rather than weakened; and the originally planned route-level edit-page test was dropped because ':id' routes do not resolve under the integration harness — a pre-existing harness gap, verified to affect the details page equally on main — so the edit path is covered at the hook level instead, which tests the same request-building logic more directly.
